dialogue.content: put my phone in a drawer for an hour.
checked it twice from across the room.
agreed to be somewhere without checking the day.
ran something for the first time and it went fine.
sorted the photos from the last thing into a folder nobody will open.
I'd have bet anything that a format which flopped once would flop again. it goes the other way — second time round nobody's performing, because everyone already knows how bad it can be.
confidently, and I was wrong about it twice.
had a coffee alone and it was the best part of the day.
someone asked how I was and I answered honestly by accident.
declined a thing politely and then felt weird about it for an hour.
tried a brand new format nobody had done before. mixed.
wrote half a message and left it in the box.
looked up how far away a place is instead of asking.
borrowed a charger and forgot to give it back. again.
watched something everyone had already discussed.
did the laundry and answered nothing for three hours.
the two things that turned into actual traditions both had a first outing everyone agreed was a disaster. the ones we dropped after one go never came back and nobody misses them.
both. the disaster seems to be load-bearing.
someone rescheduled and I was more relieved than I should admit.
stood outside a place for ten minutes before going in.
made a list of people to check on. didn't check on them.
got the train instead of driving and read most of the way.
